summary: Guided tenant live-swap to revert aggressive prefetch + q4 quant profile without full traffic cutover
description: Issue summary: CardioBridge observed elevated tail latency (95th and 99th) and a small number of truncated responses after enabling a tenant-scoped optimizer profile that combined aggressive async batching, KV prefetch, and a q4_0 quantization profile. Impact: customer-facing API latency spikes impacting SLAs for two production routes (chat-stream and generate-text) with occasional user-visible truncation. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, single tenant traffic ~350 RPS, pinned to llama-13b-q4_0 and redwood-instruct-4b-fp16. Steps to reproduce: 1) Hit /v1/generate with same request shape (avg tokens 120) against tenant api-key, 2) Observe 95p and 99p latency in Console traces and per-route dashboard, 3) Note occasional aborted streams in logs (client saw truncated outputs). Observed telemetry: - 95p latency rose from 180ms -> 520ms within 30m of enabling optimizer profile. - Increase in scheduler queue length and grab-failures in runtime logs. - Sporadic 5xx rate <0.1% but correlated with high tail latency windows. Attachments / referenced artifacts: console dashboard link (prod route): https://console.redwood.ai/d/tenant/CardioBridge/routes; relevant trace ids: trace-20260311-1a2b, trace-20260311-1a2c. Customer request: assistance performing a controlled, per-tenant rollback to the previous optimizer snapshot (pre-change) while preserving live traffic and avoiding broad capacity reallocation. They explicitly asked to avoid full tenant draining or manual re-deploy of dedicated pool.
steps_to_reproduce: Send representative requests against customer api-key hitting /v1/generate with avg token length 120
Observe per-route 95p/99p latency in Console over 15-30m window
Inspect serving-runtime logs for scheduler queue growth and KV prefetch errors
Look for truncated streaming events in api gateway / stream logs
logs_and_snippets: [2026-03-11T14:12:01Z] quant-loader: loaded profile q4_0 for model llama-13b-q4_0
attempted_mitigations: Customer rolled flag batcher.async_max_tokens from 4096 -> 2048 (no improvement)
Support temporarily set tenant traffic split 95/5 to pass small % through stable snapshot (observed partial improvement in 95p)
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: aggressive async batching increased internal queueing when prefix cache hit rates dropped due to recent prompt shape variance
Hypothesis B: q4_0 quant profile combined with KV prefetch caused increased CPU-side serialization and occasional model truncation under high concurrent KV loads
Telemetry shows correlation between prefix cache miss spikes and tail latency
runbook_recommendation: 1) Create immutable snapshot of current optimizer config for the tenant via /admin/optimizer/snapshot API
2) Prepare target stable snapshot id (the one from 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC) and verify via GET /admin/optimizer/snapshots
3) Execute staged traffic swap: 95% traffic to current profile, 5% to stable snapshot using traffic-split API on per-route basis
4) Monitor 1m/5m/15m 95p latency and trace error rate for 20m
5) If 5% shows improvement, incrementally increase to 25% then 50% before full cutover
6) If any regressions, rollback split back to 100% current snapshot and escalate to SRE
7) If final cutover succeeds, persist the stable snapshot as active and remove offender flags
requested_support_actions: Run a snapshot restore for tenant CardioBridge with id stable-snap-20260310-0900 and coordinate staged traffic split changes with the customer
Watch live metrics for 60 minutes and provide rollback throttle commands if tail latency rebounds
Open PR to add an automated safety gate that prevents aggressive prefetch + q4 profile being applied together at tenant scope
